name: Amazigh (Berber) and Saharan peoples
summary: The Amazigh (Berber) peoples of North Africa and the Sahara, including the Tuareg, who herded animals and led caravans across the desert. Rock art shows a “green Sahara” before about 3000 BCE.

knownFor.label: Tifinagh script
knownFor.note: An ancient script still used by the Tuareg.

knownFor.label: Tassili rock art
knownFor.note: Paintings of cattle, people and wild animals from the “green Sahara”, made thousands of years before the desert formed.

knownFor.label: Tagelmust (Tuareg veil)
knownFor.note: A long indigo cloth worn by Tuareg men.

location.value: Indigenous to North Africa, living across parts of Morocco, Algeria and Libya, and to a lesser extent Tunisia, Mauritania, northern Mali and northern Niger.

terrain.value: Desert, mountains (Atlas and Hoggar) and oases.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Berbers; Wikipedia: Tuareg people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

climate.value: The Sahara dried out after about 3000 BCE; hot days and cold nights.

resources.value: Oases with dates, salt, camels, goats and trade routes.

population.value: Berber languages are spoken by about 14–16 million people in Africa today.

urbanisation.value: Mostly nomadic; oasis towns such as Ghadames.

migration.value: From about 2000 BCE, Berber languages spread westward from the Nile Valley across the northern Sahara into the Maghreb.

economicBase.value: Most were farmers or semi-pastoral herders; the Tuareg are traditionally nomadic pastoralists of the Sahara.

tradeRoutes.value: Towns such as Sijilmasa and Tlemcen prospered on the main trade routes.

moneyAndTax.value: Exchange of goods; later coins from Mediterranean states.

inequality.value: Tuareg society had nobles, vassals and enslaved people.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Berbers; Wikipedia: Tuareg people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

governmentType.value: Tribes and kingdoms such as Numidia and Mauretania; the Tuareg have a king called the Amenokal.

keyRulers.value: King Masinissa, who unified Numidia and allied with Rome in the Second Punic War (218–201 BCE).

succession.value: Often through the mother’s line among the Tuareg.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Berbers; Wikipedia: Tuareg people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

armyAndTech.value: Camel riders with swords, spears and shields.

majorWars.value: Revolts against Roman rule (a great uprising in 396), the Berber Revolt of 739–740 against Arab rule, and the 1871 Kabylie revolt against French rule.

territoryChange.value: Berber dynasties such as the Almoravids and Almohads ruled much of North Africa and the Iberian Peninsula between the 11th and 16th centuries.

alliancesRivals.value: Numidian kings sided with Rome or Carthage; Masinissa allied with Rome in 206 BCE.

inventions.value: Camel saddles, water skins, oasis irrigation (foggara).

scienceEducation.value: Tifinagh script (inscriptions from the 4th–5th centuries CE); oral poetry.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Berbers; Wikipedia: Tuareg people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

openness.value: Open to trade across the desert.

communicationTransport.value: Caravans; Tuareg caravans first used oxen and horses, later camels.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Berbers; Wikipedia: Tuareg people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

religion.value: Traditional polytheist beliefs, Christianity in places, then conversion to Islam after the Arab conquests of the 7th–8th centuries.

languageWriting.value: Berber (Amazigh) languages of the Afroasiatic family; prehistoric Tifinagh inscriptions have been found.

artsArchitecture.value: Rock paintings such as those of Tassili n’Ajjer and Tadrart Acacus; traditional silver jewellery.

socialStructure.value: Many groups such as Kabyles, Chaouis, Rifians and Tuareg; Tuareg society is very hierarchical.

sharedIdentity.value: The name Amazigh, used since antiquity; a modern Berber Culture Movement promotes a shared Amazigh identity.

dailyLife.value: Tents covered with animal skins or mats (goatskin tents among some groups).
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Berbers; Wikipedia: Tuareg people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

neighbours.value: Carthage, Rome, the Byzantines, Vandals, Arabs, Ottomans and Sudanic empires.

ideasReligions.value: Islam and Arabic spread among the Berbers after the Arab conquests of the 7th and 8th centuries.

colonisation.value: North Africa came under French, Spanish and Italian colonial rule; the French defeated the Ahaggar Tuareg in 1902.

riseSignals.value: Control of desert routes and oases.

peakPeriod.value: Trans-Saharan trade at its height, about 800–1500.

declineSignals.value: Trade shifted to Atlantic sea routes after 1500.

outcome.value: Berbers still live across North Africa; Berber became an official language in Morocco (2011) and Algeria (2016).

overallCertainty.value: Mostly known from outsiders’ records and archaeology.
